subject: tokens
lesson: Review events repeat the same full key often (176 of 322 model reviews, 56% of review tokens), so check carry() before you tune the review_item constant.
proposal:
Make two changes in parityctl/repair.py.

1. At load time, compute review_item from the ledger. Use the median of the review events that have tokens.total > 0 and verdict accept or reject. Leave out precheck-only events and carried events. Use the constant only as a fallback when there are fewer than 30 events. Today this gives 8,046, so set the fallback to 8000 and change the comment.

2. At repair.py:699, count only the items whose (bundle, checker, review) digest will change. Count carried and precheck-reject items as 0 tokens. This matches what cardrun.carry() does.

Expected gain:
- (a) makes the cost of each repair round correct to about 1k tokens per item, and the engine stops repairing review_other items, which lose about 1k tokens each. This gain is small.
- The larger gain comes from making sure carry() runs on every review. The engine then does not review the same full key again. In the measured data this saves up to 0.90M of 1.75M non-test review tokens (51.5%). This is about 2.8k tokens per reviewed item, or about 3.3k per accepted item (275 accepts) ❓.
- Check this with a test: run the review twice on the same proof. The second run must write carried_from on all items and use 0 review tokens.

subject: hard
lesson: Triage confidence is explained lines divided by changed lines (triage.py:323), so it measures coverage and not correctness; do not use a fixed 0.5 cut until each cause has labelled cases.
proposal:
Mine labelled cases automatically from runs that already exist, then use the labels to decide when to show a hint. Do not use a fixed 0.5 threshold.

1. Add `triage.py mine-cases` (new code next to cmd_validate at triage.py:630).
   - Take neighbouring pairs from the 114 stored funcdiff build folders under /data/parity-v2.
   - Keep each function that goes from DIFF (score >= 85) to MATCH.
   - Get the source change from `git diff` between the two bns-lift revisions (the `rev` file of each run) for that function only.
   - Give a label from simple rules on that change:
     - A new or renamed global, string or vtable symbol: data_ref.
     - A call that was added or removed: missing_call or extra_call.
     - A changed number in an argument: constant.
     - A changed `>> 16`, `HIWORD` or `(WORD)`: hiword.
     - An if/else swap: branch_inversion.
     - Any other change: needs a manual label.
   - Write the result as triage-cases.json rows with `"source": "mined"`.
   - Work through the causes in this order: data_ref (46 low, 0 cases), constant (58, 1), missing_call (18, 0), hiword (13, 0).
   - Goal: at least 10 cases per cause. The gate below needs that many. No new builds are needed.

2. Add a calibration table, triage-calibration.json, per cause.
   - Measure the cause's precision on the validation set.
   - Also measure precision against the margin: (lines the winning cause explains − lines the second cause explains) / changed lines.
   - Today the second cause nearly ties with the winner in 52 of 64 constant items and in 47 of 55 data_ref items. That near-tie is the case to suppress.

3. Gate the hint in `_result` (triage.py:346).
   - Show the hint only when the cause has at least 10 labelled cases, precision of at least 0.7, and a margin above the calibrated cut.
   - In all other cases, give the cause family (layout, call, constant or data from FAMILY at triage.py:59) and the two best causes as "unverified". Do not give a one-line fix order.
   - Change ease() (triage.py:404) to multiply by the calibrated precision, not by the raw confidence. Then correct low-confidence hints, such as tail_merge at 0.13 with 2 of 2 exact, do not drop down the fix list.

Expected gain:
- About 255 hints get either a measured precision or the "unverified" label. Agents no longer act on unmeasured one-line orders. ❓ (estimate)
- Suppose 30 % of the unmeasured hints are wrong. That is about the rate of non-exact verdicts today (2 of 9). Then roughly 75 wasted DIFF rebuilds stop for each full pass over the list. ❓
- Validation grows from 9 cases to a few hundred without new builds. ❓ The exact count depends on how many DIFF→MATCH pairs the 114 runs hold.
- Cost: one script of about 150 lines, plus manual review of the "needs a manual label" rows. The mined cases add about 1–2 k tokens to triage-cases.json for every 50 cases. ❓

subject: ops
lesson: Check that sched.LIMIT_RE matches each text in quota.BILLING and quota.LIMIT, because a limit text that only quota.classify knows counts against --retries and parks the card when no PAUSE file is present.
proposal:
Make quota.py the one source for limit texts.

1. In quota.py, add a public function `is_limit_text(text)`. It returns True when the text matches any entry in BILLING or LIMIT, or matches RETRY_ONLY = ('rate limit', 'overloaded', '429', 'credential broker'). Use \b boundaries for 429.
2. In sched.py:97-98, delete the hand-written list. Build the pattern from the quota lists: LIMIT_RE = re.compile('|'.join(map(re.escape, quota.BILLING + quota.LIMIT)) + r'|\b429\b|rate limit|overloaded|credential broker|\b402\b|payment', re.I).
3. Keep the existing negative test: cardrun's text "killed, provider paused or tool error" must not match.
4. In tests/test_operator.py, add a parity test. For each entry in quota.BILLING + quota.LIMIT, assert that sched.LIMIT_RE matches it. For a list of real CLI strings ("You've hit your limit · resets 5pm", "session limit reached", "weekly limit reached", "out of extra usage", "insufficient_quota", "HTTP 402 Payment Required"), assert that quota.classify(...) is not None implies LIMIT_RE matches.

Risk: bare 'quota' becomes a match. A card-fault text that contains "quota" then waits as a limit and does not count. LIMIT_CAP=48 (sched.py:100) limits that loop, so a false match cannot loop forever.

Expected gain: the 11 known limit and billing texts that now go unmatched stop using up --retries. Their cards no longer park when no PAUSE file is present (expired, deleted, write failed, or standalone sched). With no operator, a limit that lasts longer than 2 retries no longer parks good cards. Each such card no longer needs a manual `sched unpark --reset`. The change is about 10 lines in sched.py plus one test. It costs nothing at run time.

subject: quality
lesson: A review receipt counts only when its review_digest equals the sha256 of the current review.py, so any edit to review.py makes all stored accept receipts give zero credit.
proposal:
Do not add a credit rule to proof.py. The evidence rejects that option.

**Change:** In feedback.py:526, fit p_new on credited MATCHes and not on raw NOREF MATCHes. That is: p_new = (auto credited + accepted review items) / ids_total. Count an item that has no receipt as not credited until it gets a decision.

**Where the data is:** The credited count is already in each card record ('credited', feedback.py:174-182). The fit must use that count, not ids_match_noref.

**Expected gain:** The p_new of handler cards falls. Real credit per raw new MATCH is 0.43 for gap24, 0.56 for gap23, 0.75 for gap26 and 0.71 for gap19. The job cards gap01 to gap05 stay between 0.81 and 1.00. Today the ranking gives handler cards such as gap-24 and gap-26 (PLAN-NEXT rows 4 and 6) about 1.3 to 2 times more credit than the reviews support ❓ (I did not re-run the ranking). The selection will then prefer job and core cards.

**Second change, needed for correctness:** Every stored accept receipt has an old review digest. check_review therefore counts 0 of the 62 accepts today. Before more review spend, re-run the review of the 62 accepted items with the current review.py, or keep review.py unchanged during a wave. If you do not, the review tokens give no credit.

subject: tokens
lesson: The stream-json assistant events carry only a stub output_tokens for each message id, so a live StreamMeter cost reads 30-40 % too low until the result event arrives.
proposal:
## Proposal: give StreamMeter the true output count, and stop a `result` line from tripping the cap

### Change 1. Read the final output count while the session runs (parityctl/author.py)
- Add `--include-partial-messages` to `CLAUDE_FLAGS` (author.py:125-126).
- In `StreamMeter.feed` (author.py:357-373), handle `type == 'stream_event'` lines where `event.type == 'message_delta'`. Each such event has the running output count of the current message. Keep `self.out_live[current_id] = max(old, event.usage.output_tokens)`. Take `current_id` from the `message_start` stream event before it.
- In `cost()`, `total()` and `tokens()` (no-result branch), use `max(stub, out_live[id])` for `output_tokens` of each message.
- ❓ I did not check that the CLI passes `message_delta` through in `stream_event`. Check it with one more dry run (fable-tokens/dry/run.py). Pass condition: the stream sum is within 1 % of `result.usage.output_tokens`.
- If the CLI does not pass it through, use this fallback. Make authproxy.py read `usage.output_tokens` from each `message_delta` SSE event that it forwards. Have it append `{msg_id, output_tokens}` to a side file that the runner reads.

### Change 2. Do not let the `result` line trip the cap (author.py:458-461)
- Run the cap check only while `meter.result is None`. When the session has already ended with `subtype == 'success'`, give the status `ok`. If the final cost is over the cap, write the overrun in `reason`.
- Do not apply this change to the card cap (author.py:1040). The card cap must still use the final cost.

### Change 3. Mark partial rows until change 1 is verified
- In the no-result branch of `tokens()`, set `output_tokens` to the stream sum × 31 or leave it as it is, and keep `partial=True`. The ledger reader must not add partial rows to cost-per-MATCH figures without a note.

### Expected gain
| Item | Now | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live cost error | −30 % to −39 % (2 sessions) | about 0 % ❓ (with message_delta) |
| Real stop point at token_cap 1,200,000 | about 1.7M to 2.0M real units ❓ (×1.43-1.65) | 1.2M ± one message |
| A finished session that ends over the cap | Parked as `token_cap` (author.py:1035-1037) | `ok`, with the overrun in `reason` |
| Output in partial ledger rows | about 3 % of true | true |
| WAVES-VS-V2 119k/181k per MATCH | not affected | no change needed |

Do not change the tokens-per-MATCH figure. Do not raise or lower the `token_cap` value now. Change 1 fixes the meter, so the present cap number becomes correct with no change to its value.

subject: ops
lesson: In sched.py, a host or scheduler crash during a cardrun gives rc=None, which maps to rc=2 'process gone' and calls retry(), so it uses up a card's --retries budget and parks the card on crash 3.
proposal: In parityctl/sched.py Sched.finished, add a crash-wait branch after the pause block at line 432. If rc was None (or rc<0 from a signal) and the cardrun result is 'running' or 'landing', and r['crash_waits'] < CRASH_CAP (new constant, 6, next to LIMIT_CAP at :100), then increment crash_waits. Set not_before=now()+retry_delay. Set the phase to 'retry' with crash=True. Keep landing unchanged and return without a call to retry(). Set crash_waits back to 0 where retries go back to 0 (:444, :485, :496, unpark :805). Add 2 tests next to test_sched.py:375. Test 1: 3 crashes give retries 0, not parked, landing True. Test 2: CRASH_CAP+1 crashes give a park. Gain: with --retries 2, a card survives 6 crashes instead of 2, and keeps its full retry budget for real failures. Each crash that this path absorbs removes one manual 'sched unpark' and one queue stall for that card. A real crash loop still parks after 6 crashes.

subject: hard
lesson: Before you treat a triage item as a source bug, compare the same function in the other exes' funcdiff.json: a DIFF in one exe that is MATCH elsewhere comes from per-exe LTCG, so a body edit changes every exe.
proposal:
Add a cross-exe split flag in triage.py. Do not add a skip.

1. After the per-exe loop in triage() (triage.py:537-565), find each function name that is DIFF in exe X and MATCH in another exe. Use the funcdiff.json files that the loop already loads in `ref`. Keep one ref dict for each exe. Then set detail.cross_exe_split = {'match_in': [...], 'diff_in': [...]}. Also flag groups like SetInvalidInfo: same function, DIFF in 2 or more exes, and scores that differ by 2 or more points (96.3 against 93.3).

2. Change ease(): if cross_exe_split is set and the cause is in the layout family (tail_merge, branch_inversion, instruction_order) or is register_swap, multiply the ease by 0.3. Do not lower call_target, missing_call or extra_call items. For these, noinline on the callee is a proven fix (ranks 6 and 7).

3. Change hint(): for split items, return "per-exe LTCG split: same object is MATCH in <exes>. A body reshape changes all exes. Try __declspec(noinline) on <moved/surplus callee> once, else accept the MATCH exes and park <exe>". For vendor paths (vendor/zstd), return "per-exe LTCG tail merge in vendor code: no source fix; park".

4. Add a rule in the card or review step: when a build raises N exes to MATCH and lowers 1 exe, keep the gain and park the lower exe with reason 'per_exe_ltcg'. Do not revert the build.

Expected gain, measured:
- 9 of 43 tail_merge items get an honest hint. These are the 5 split items plus the 4 SetInvalidInfo items.
- Feedback line 18 changes from WRONG to accept: +3 MATCH (CG, SCD, POD) and 1 LD park. It is not a revert.
- Over all causes, 54 items get the flag. About 30 of them (layout family, register_swap, data_ref) move lower in the fix list ❓. data_ref is not in the layout family, so check the multiply rule against it before you ship.
- The labelled cases are a 'duplicates' item (SetInvalidInfo) and 'shares' items (addNode, ZSTD x3).
- The 33 single-exe tail_merge items, which include ranks 17 and 21, do not change. Their failures (wrong cause on line 12, compiler merge on line 31) need better cause detection, not this flag.

The ranking effect is small. The split tail_merge items are already at ranks 151 to 312 (ease 0.05 or less). So most of the gain comes from step 4 and the hint, not from step 2.

subject: quality
lesson: Before you blame a proof rule on the card's own edit, run git log -S on the scratch clone, because an earlier commit in the same card (for example 4f7958c, which removes /INCLUDE pragmas) can cause the failure.
proposal:
Add a `precheck` step to cardrun.py. Also run a lost-match check right after the full build.

1. **New step `precheck`.** Add it to CHECK_STEPS (cardrun.py:116). Call it at cardrun.py:1074, after plan and before gate. On `base..rev` it runs these checks, with git only:
   - `proof.pinned()` for each path in `proof.changed_paths()` (R2).
   - `proof.cmake_violations()` (R3).
   - `guard.check_source()` (R7). Today R7 runs only inside proof.
   - A new guard rule `include_removed`. It finds `-#pragma comment(linker,"/INCLUDE:<mangled>")` lines whose symbol is MATCH in `Docs/Parity/baseline/<exe>.json` at the base commit. It is a warning, not a failure: it was right for 3 of 5 symbols in 4f7958c. The step writes the list into the error text for the author.

   A failure in R2, R3 or R7 raises `StepFail(blocked)` with the rule, path and line. All three checks reuse the existing proof and guard code. cardrun.py is not in proof.CHECKERS, so checker_digest does not change and no stored receipt goes stale.

2. **Early R1.** In the step loop, right after `full_build` (cardrun.py:1075-1080), call `proof.judge_exe(exe, baseline, signals)` with no strict data. If any `lost_match` is found, stop before base_build and strict. Name the symbols, and name a matching removed /INCLUDE from step 1 when there is one.

3. **One CMake rule.** guard.py:472 and validate_edit.py:52 allow a trailing `# comment`, but proof.py:58 does not. Make the precheck error say "remove the trailing comment". Change CMAKE_OK only in a planned checker-digest bump.

Expected gain, from the data: 2 of these 3 cases (04c cmake_edit, the 04b checker_edit part) fail in less than 1 s with 0 builds. In those runs, the work wasted before the proof failed was about 26 min (04b) and 1 build plus a strict run (04c). In all 85 stored proofs, 3 of the 9 failures are static-only, and all 3 would fail at precheck. gap17 would stop after the build: that saves base_build (about 50 s) plus strict and proof, and the author gets the exact cause (the /INCLUDE removal) instead of 'gone'. strict_regress (04b) stays a late rule. The diff does not predict it: the two functions are not in the diff, and 28 unrelated functions changed fingerprint.

subject: ops
lesson: In cardrun land, land_backup runs after land_push in the same try block, so a sync.sh failure marks a pushed card as failed (exit 2), and landq then marks it FAILED and the operator parks it.
proposal:
## Proposal: once the push is done, the land counts. landq owns one backup, and the backup can fail without harm.

### Changes

| # | Where | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `cardrun.py` `land()` (1175-1185) | Move `land_backup` out of the `try` that sets 'failed'. After `land_push` is done, run it in its own `try`. On StepFail, keep the step record as `failed`, set `st['backup_pending'] = why[:300]`, call `finish('landed', '')` and return 0. A backup failure never changes the result of a land after the push. |
| 2 | `cardrun.py` CLI and `s_backup` (1382-1392) | Add `land --backup {run,defer}`. The default is `run`, which sched cardrun mode uses. With `defer`, `s_backup` returns `{'deferred': 'landq'}` and does not run sync.sh. |
| 3 | `landq.py` `cardrun()` (~633) | When `self.s.get('backup')` is set, pass `--backup defer` to `land`. This gives one sync.sh run for each land, in `finish`. |
| 4 | `landq.py` `finish` (811-813) | On rc≠0, set `extra['backup_pending']=True` and keep the land LANDED. At the start of each `landq run`, if any LANDED entry has `backup_pending`, run sync.sh **once** for all of them. Clear the flags on rc 0. Use `--retries` and the repair path for none of this. |
| 5 | `landq.py` `land_steps` / `recover_steps` (597-624, 569-590), and `sched.phase` (589) | Add a recovery rule: if the cardrun state has `steps.land_push.status == 'done'`, call `finish()` (landq) or `landed()` (sched). Do this even when `result == 'failed'`. This also repairs the 5 existing cards with full credit, not through `landed_on_main` with no credit. |
| 6 | `backup/sync.sh` | Wrap the git part in `flock "$ENGINE/.git/sync.lock"`. Before you push, run `git fetch` and `git pull --rebase` for `backup-live`. These fix the observed causes: `index.lock` (gap-07) and non-fast-forward (gap-08, gap-19). |

### Tests to add

All tests use a stub `run_cmd`:
1. Push done and backup exit 3: the result is `landed`, rc is 0, and `backup_pending` is set.
2. A landq land with backup set: sync.sh runs exactly 1 time.
3. A cardrun state `failed` with `land_push` done: landq.finish runs and records the credit. sched marks the card landed and its dependants start.

### Expected gain

| Item | Now | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| False FAILED or park after a real push | 5 of 24 lands (21 %), and each needed a human | 0 |
| Dependants blocked behind a parked card | yes | no |
| sync.sh runs (commits and pushes) per landq land | 2 | 1 (fewer when lands are batched) |
| Land wall time spent in backup | median 5.8 s, worst 607 s | 0 s inside cardrun land, and one run after it |
| Credit on a recovered land | lost (`landed_on_main` path) | kept (`finish` path) |

Model tokens saved directly: about 0 ❓. The gain is in human interventions and lander time. This follows the audit gap 16 rule (a limit must not park a good card) and closes the backup part of audit gap 10.

subject: tools
lesson: In ledger.py backfill_events, the cost of proof_index is the deep rglob walk under gap/ (about 195 s), not the hashing (83 files, 869,407 bytes, about 0 s); a glob at most 3 levels deep finds the same 83 files in under 1 s.
proposal: In parityctl/ledger.py, replace proof_index with resolve_proofs(need, data, ledger_paths), and make backfill_events read the review rows first to build the set of needed digests. resolve_proofs reads the cardrun state.json proof paths, then globs proof*.json at most 3 levels down under gap/ and cardrun/, then globs proof*.json and probe*.json in each ledger's directory and its parent. It stops when the set is empty, and it runs the full rglob only for digests that are still missing. backfill_events gives the warning 'proof not found <pd12> for <rel>' for each digest that is not found. Expected gain: the lookup time drops from 195.2 s to under 1 s. All 13 keys become complete; the 5 broken events are fixed only after they are re-keyed or superseded. Keep test_backfill_is_idempotent_and_marks_estimates (parityctl/tests/test_ledger.py:407) and test_gap06_ledger_in_backfill green. Add test_backfill_hashes_only_needed_proofs. It puts decoy proofs in a deep directory and a probe-*.json file next to a fix ledger. It asserts four things: no decoy is hashed, the probe proof is found, all keys are complete, and a missing digest gives exactly one warning.

subject: tools
lesson: The run_cmd call at cardrun.py:454 has no timeout and no code kills a live hung child, so a hung land_backup rsync held slot 4 for 2,654 s and 5,524 s until a manual SIGTERM, and the ledger does not record that kill.
proposal:
Give each command a wall-clock limit in run_cmd. When the limit passes, kill the process group, then raise StepFail.

1. Timeout table. Rule: about 3 × p95, with a floor of 300 s. Key the table on the command name, not the step name, because base_build also runs the full_build command.

| Command | p95 / max (s) | Limit (s) |
|---|---|---|
| gate | 3 / 4.9 | 300 |
| full_build | 624 / 780 | 1,900 |
| strict (per exe) | 49 / 65 | 300 |
| proof, toolslane | 1.1 / 6.6 | 300 |
| review | 236 (log p95 375) / 728 | 1,800 |
| parity_accept | 0.9 / 17.5 | 300 |
| backup | done runs: p50 5.8, max 607 | 900 |
| network git (push, fetch, clone) | 2.9 / 3.3 | 120 |
| local git | — | 60 |
| landq.py:337 (cardrun land) | — | total of the inner limits + 300, so 3,000 |

2. Config place:
- Put a `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS` dict in cardrun.py next to COMMANDS (cardrun.py:130).
- Override it with the key `step_timeout` in build.json, read through BUILD.
- Override it again with `timeouts` in the --config JSON, which load_config reads (cardrun.py:277). The tests use this level.
- Do not use build_client.json, because the x86 checker digest includes it.

3. Code change in run_cmd (cardrun.py:453-457):
- Start the command with `Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, env=e, stdout=f, stderr=STDOUT, start_new_session=True)`.
- Call `p.wait(timeout=limit)`.
- On TimeoutExpired: send `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGTERM)`, wait 10 s, then send `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGKILL)` and call `p.wait()`. Write the line `cardrun: TIMEOUT after N s (limit L)` to the log. Raise `StepFail('command %s timed out after %d s (limit %d, log %s)', blocked=False)`.
- Wrap the wait in `try/except BaseException`, and kill the group there too. The reason: with a new session, the SIGTERM that slotq forwards and the terminal's SIGINT no longer reach the grandchildren.

4. Same change for the helpers:
- Add `timeout=` to the git helpers at cardrun.py:248, landq.py:154, queue_build.py:159 and operator_run.py:153. Use 120 s when args[0] is push, fetch or clone, else 60 s.
- Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ServerAliveInterval=15'` in each of these git helpers.
- Convert TimeoutExpired to the local error type: StepFail, EntryStop('FAILED') or Refused.
- Use the same Popen, new session, then killpg pattern at landq.py:337 (3,000 s) and landq.py:869 (900 s).
- Optional: add a `--max-seconds` option to slotrun and pass it to `child.wait(timeout)` at slotq.py:1162.

5. Test: add `test_step_timeout_kills_group_and_fails` in tests/test_cardrun.py.
- The stub `backup` command starts `sleep 60` as a grandchild, writes the grandchild pid to a file, then sleeps 60 s.
- Set `timeouts: {backup: 2}` in the test config.
- Call run_cmd('backup', 'land_backup') on the runner.
- Assert that StepFail comes back in less than 2 + 5 s.
- Assert that `blocked is False` and that the message holds 'timed out' and the log path.
- Assert that the log ends with the TIMEOUT line.
- Assert that `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises ProcessLookupError for the stub pid and for the grandchild pid.

Expected gain:
- The 2 killed backups held slot 4 for 2,654 s and 5,524 s (8,178 s in total), with no error text, until someone killed them.
- With a 900 s limit, each fails by itself at 900 s, with the log path in `why`. Slot time saved: 6,378 s. No operator action is necessary.
- The limits are at least 2.4× the largest good run (full_build 1,900 vs 780; review 1,800 vs 728; backup 900 vs 607), so the fix does not kill good builds.

A separate root cause needs its own fix: sync.sh copies nested `backup/state` trees, which made a 134 MB log. Add an rsync exclude for `*/backup/state/`. ❓ I did not verify this exclude against sync.sh:30.

subject: quality
lesson: A --no-packet card never gets shards (author.py:1230 needs self.packet), and handoff_text (author.py:1042-1067) keeps no function list or facts, so a card with more than about 10 functions must be sharded from its "### N." evidence headings before round 1.

## Shard --no-packet cards by evidence headings, at most 8 functions per shard

1. **New function:** add `card_shards(card_text, max_funcs=8, budget=80000)` in parityctl/author_packet.py next to `filter_card` (line 274).
   - It parses the `### N. EXE \`rva\` \`name\`` headings in `## Evidence`. It also parses the matching rows of `## Functions in scope` and `## Misses`.

   - Each shard keeps the card head (goal, rules, batch notes) and only its own evidence blocks. It adds one line: "(N functions of this card are not shown. Another session does them.)".

2. **Driver change:** in author.py `s_packet` (line 900), when `packet` is off, set `self.packet = {'shards': card_shards(self.text), 'tokens': …, 'kind': 'card'}`.

4. **No change:** author.py:1230-1252 and the no_change park at :1027-1028 stay as they are.

**Expected gain (❓ estimates):**

- **lg-01:** a 3-shard run replaces a 417,607-unit park with no edit. Each shard costs about 150-200k units, like cg-01 (197k for 10 functions).
- **pod-01:** the fix removes the about 319k-unit re-read in the x01 split.
- **crypto-01 (35 functions) and shared-01 (56 functions):** each card gets 5 or 7 sessions below 80k. This avoids a probable 300-420k-unit park per card ❓.
- **Batch total:** about 1.0-1.5 M cost units saved over the 6 cards (162 items), and all 162 items get an author session with an edit.

**Test:** run lg-01 again. The fix works if each shard session makes its first Edit before 80k prompt tokens and no split fires.

subject: tools
lesson: Before you build a shared helper that checker modules import, look at proof.CHECKERS, because an edit to that helper changes checker behaviour but does not change the checker digest.
proposal:
**What to add.** Add a new module `parityctl/gitx.py`. Do NOT add it to CHECKERS. It has one function:

`run(repo, *args, read=False, check=True, text=True, env=None, inp=None, err=RuntimeError)`

**Default env.**
- Start from os.environ.
- Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
- Put `-c core.quotepath=off` in argv.
- When `read=True`, also set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
- Merge the caller's `env` last.

**Stderr rule.** On a non-zero exit with check=True, raise `err(msg)`. The message is:

`'git %s in %s exit %d: %s' % (' '.join(args[:3]), repo, rc, (stderr or stdout).strip()[-300:])`

The exception also carries `.stderr` and `.returncode` as attributes.

**Return value.**
- check=True: stripped str, or bytes when text=False.
- check=False: the CompletedProcess.

**How each caller keeps its own error type.** Pass a factory as `err`:
- cardrun: `err=StepFail`
- landq: `err=lambda m: EntryStop('FAILED', m)`
- canary, operator_run, land86: `err=Refused`
- clientrun: `err=Fail`
- opstatus: `check=False`, then return None when rc != 0.

**Order of the switch.**
1. cardrun: 28 helper calls, plus the 5 raw subprocess calls. Mark 1195 and 1444 `read=True`.
2. landq: 22 calls.
3. queue_build (862 `read=True`), operator_run (637 `read=True`) and integrate. integrate is not a checker, and today it loses stderr.
4. author, repair, pilot, canary.
5. opstatus, remote_build, clientrun, land86, evidence, triage.
6. Leave reclaim_plan and import_state as they are. They are sealed read-only on purpose.
7. Archive fix6_bench, but first do the L2 grep.

**Checkers.** Leave guard.py, proof.py, buildonce.py and toolslane.py on their own helpers. Move them only in a CHECKERS edit that is already planned, and then add gitx.py to CHECKERS in the same change.

**Fix the guard stderr loss now, at its callers.** These files are not checkers, so there is no rebuild:
- cardrun.py:1415 and cardrun.py:1553: when exc is a CalledProcessError, add `exc.stderr.decode(errors='replace')[-300:]` to the message.
- landq.py:547: do the same.

**Test.** Add `tests/test_gitx.py` with these cases:
1. A failing `git rev-parse nosuchref` raises the given `err` type. The message holds `nosuchref` and git's `fatal:` text.
2. A file named `é.txt` comes back from `ls-files` as `é.txt`, not as `"\303\251.txt"`.
3. After `touch` changes the stat data of a tracked file, `run(repo, 'status', read=True)` does not create `index.lock` and does not change the index mtime.
4. While a test holds `index.lock` (os.open with O_EXCL), `run(read=True)` still succeeds and leaves the lock in place.
5. Add `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to the env check, with a fake https remote and a `fetch` that must fail fast.

**Expected gain.**
- 15 helper copies in non-checker modules go away, about 60-90 tokens each, so about 1,100 tokens in total.

subject: ops
lesson: A failed backup after a done push is never retried on the sched path. The landq retry_backups runs under the landq lock with no timeout and no try limit. sync.sh exits 0 when every push fails.
proposal: Add backup_retry(op) in operator_run.py. Call it once per tick, outside the landq lock. It reads the sched st['cards'][*].backup_pending flags and the landq LANDED backup_pending entries. It runs sync.sh once with timeout=1200 s and GIT_SSH_COMMAND with ServerAliveInterval=30. Exit 0 clears all flags. Exit 4, index.lock or a timeout adds 1 to backup_tries and retries on the next tick. Exit 3, key-guard exit 1, backup_tries>=3 or more than 6 h pending sets heartbeat backup_blocked, shows it in status_text and sends one ntfy alert; lands continue. Remove retry_backups from Lander.run. Defer the backup in Lander.finish too, so sync.sh never runs under the landq lock. In sync.sh, make the failed backup-live push exit 5, and make the not-on-main case exit non-zero, so a push failure is seen. Add a canary mode backup-fail: the stub exits 3 once then 0, and in a second case it sleeps past the timeout. Invariant: every backup_pending is cleared or escalated before the run ends, and no land waits more than T for the landq lock. Gain: the sched path gets its first retry; the land queue cannot be blocked by sync.sh; exits 3 and 1 reach a human within 3 tries; push failures become visible; the canary covers the path.

subject: tools
lesson: Run the schema of a SQLite ledger only when PRAGMA user_version is old, and before you switch a ledger to WAL, change backup/sync.sh: today it copies only *.sqlite files, so it does not copy the -wal file.
proposal:
Add parityctl/dbx.py. It is not in proof.CHECKERS (proof.py:63-65), and review_digest does not hash file bytes, so no digest changes. API: dbx.connect(path, role, schema=None, user_version=0).

1. Roles:

| Role | Open | Wait | Pragmas |
|---|---|---|---|
| reader | file:…?mode=ro, isolation_level=None | busy_timeout 5,000 ms (web 2,000 ms) | none, read-only |
| writer | isolation_level=None | busy_timeout 30,000 ms | journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL; a helper `with dbx.tx(db):` runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE…COMMIT/ROLLBACK for every read-then-write (receipts.*, events._insert, leases.claim/finish, pilot.put) |
| schema | as writer | as writer | run SCHEMA only when PRAGMA user_version < N, inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then set user_version=N; also cache it once per process for each realpath |

Wrap OperationalError as dbx.LockError('<role> <path>: database is locked after <n> s'). Then a card step fails with a message that names the file and the role. Fix score.py:101 and events.py:235 so they catch only 'no such table' and re-raise a lock error.

2. Fix backup/sync.sh first, before any WAL switch. Snapshot each *.sqlite with sqlite3 backup() into the backup tree, or run wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before the rsync. Without this step, WAL loses commits from the 109 tracked backup ledgers.

3. Switch order:
   1. receipts.connect (this covers cardrun ×9, landq ×5, review ×2, integrate, canary).
   2. landq.py:227/585 → role=reader (they only read).
   3. events.connect (sched, operator_run, integrate, pilot) and the ro readers in opstatus and web.
   4. leases.connect (default isolation and ALTER → schema role with user_version).
   5. pilot.Ledger.
   6. The read-only tools: ledger.py, repair.py, reclaim_plan.py, score.py, client_backup.py.

4. Add tests/test_dbx.py:
   - One process holds a read transaction for 3 s while 4 writer processes each append 200 receipts through receipts.record_review. Assert 0 'database is locked' errors, 800 rows at the end, a reader count that does not change inside its transaction, and a max writer wait under 0.5 s.
   - A schema connect on an existing ledger does not change the file change counter.
   - Two processes run the leases schema upgrade on an old file at the same time, and neither gets 'duplicate column'.
   - A forced lock error gives a dbx.LockError text that names the path.

Expected gains (measured on a tmpfs copy):
- The writer stall behind a 3 s reader drops from 3.07–3.45 s to ≤0.058 s.
- Polling-reader errors drop from 3/288 to 0/1,194.
- Connect cost drops from about 4.4 ms to about 0.24 ms, which saves about 66 ms per card over 16 connects.
- A lock fault becomes a named error. Today it is a silent 0 or empty set at events.py:235 and score.py:101, or a bare 503 from web.py.
- The speed gain is small. The main value is lock robustness and clear errors.

subject: tools
lesson: Check the CHECKERS list at the commit that changed the cardrun full_build command, because the gate script that cardrun runs was outside the digest from 2026-11-25T20:07Z (d0f0a78e) to 2026-11-26T01:47Z (da7e7c9d).
proposal:
Fix: compute the digest from a closure, and do it in a new module, parityctl/checkerset.py.

1. Owner. checkerset.py owns the digest. proof.checker_digest() returns checkerset.digest(). proof86 and cardrun keep their calls.

2. What the digest hashes:
   - Roots (declared in checkerset.py): proof.py, toolslane.py, strict.py, cfgcheck.py, and the target gate scripts from targets/<t>.json (gates.fast, gates.ref, gates.noref).
   - The Python import closure of the roots, found with AST. checkerset.py is also in the closure.
   - The script closure, found with the regex that buildonce.script_files already uses, `(\$p|\$live|/parityctl)/X`, plus every file in each dir on the sandbox PATH (gate_shims/, link_shims/).
   - DECLARED_CONFIG: the values of targets/server.json gates, compare and binaries, and the build.json keys that reach a sandbox.
   - The patched proof.EXES and guard.CONFIG after target.patch_frozen.
   - Normalised content: the Python AST with docstrings removed, and the scripts with comment lines removed. A comment edit then does not change the digest.

3. No loop. checkerset.py stores no digest value, so hashing its own bytes is safe. The LEGACY adopt list lives in checkers-legacy.json. That file is not hashed. Each entry gives (old digest, new digest, commit, reason), the same pattern as review.adopt_legacy. Seed it with b50eece0 and 105fb472.

4. Two cache fixes in the same change:
   - Add sha(funcdiff_cached.py) to fd_key (buildcache.py:787).
   - Add the checker digest to cardrun.tool_digest (cardrun.py:636). Then base strict data cannot outlive a gate change.

5. Tests:
   - tests/test_proof.py::test_checker_closure_is_hashed. It parses the imports of the roots and the script calls in the gate scripts. It fails when a reached local file is not in the digest set and not in ALLOW. ALLOW is a dict of file to reason, for example full-reference log: summary only, new_credit=False. Today the test would fail on atomicio, disk_guard, quota, target, uvsite, gate_shims/*, link_shims/* and build-noref.sh.
   - test_comment_edit_keeps_digest
   - test_fd_key_hashes_wrapper
   - test_legacy_file_not_hashed

6. Replace tests/test_proof.py:316 (fixed name list) with the closure test.

Expected gain:
- 13 or more more files and 3 config groups are covered.
- The 20:07-01:47 class of drift becomes a test failure.
- The cost side stays the same as today or gets smaller: 0 of 9 past changes were comment-only, and 2 of 9 can be adopted through LEGACY.

subject: hard
lesson: Run triage again on the current main REF build before you sort a DIFF band, because 18 of the 116 functions below the cut are already MATCH at 6824f3d.
proposal:
Change: add a structural band to parityctl/triage.py and a park list that the scheduler obeys.
1. Run triage again on the current main REF build first (rev >= 6824f3d, not eb68b2a). This removes 18 of the 116 at once.
2. Add triage.band_items() for DIFF items with score < MIN_SCORE. It uses only data that triage already loads (insn_diff.Differ + funcdiff Image). It sets one class per item, in this order:
   - STUB-CALLEE: the lift lines call import:abort. Route: plan_cards (lift the callee).
   - EMPTY: the lift has 2 or fewer insns, or the lift RVA is in an ICF group with more than 2 names. Route: stub or gap card.
   - PATH-LITERAL: every changed line is a path string. Route: one lead edit with a per-exe define (pattern fdf9041).
   - SHARED-SRC: the same key is DIFF with the same score in 3 or more exes. Route: one card per family, judged in all exes.
   - EH: the handler name or the FuncInfo maxState from .pdata/.xdata differs. This is a new 30-line reader. Route: lead fix, as in 40e2d6b/4304680.
   - FOLDED: the orig RVA has 2 or more plain names. Route: refuse credit.
   - Else AGENT, with the hint 'inline ratio X, callee only on side Y'.
3. Write the non-AGENT items to triage-latest.json 'park' with their class and route. Make slotq/author.py and plan_cards skip parked keys for author cards. Also let mkproof.py feed unmatchable-draft entries into the same park list, so that the draft has an engine use.
Expected gain:
- 46 of 116 go to agents (35 after the rebase), not 116. With about 6 functions and about 20 builds per card, this saves about 230 builds per round ❓.
- One lead edit for PATH-LITERAL can give +12 LD MATCH. The EH lead form has already given LG/SCD wmain MATCH.
